security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, example fetch calls, and standard server-side JWT secret usage. The meaningful risk is that the skill includes npm/npx setup guidance and a PowerShell bootstrap script that can install packages and create or modify files. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, obfuscation, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Bootstrap and setup guidance uses @latest or @canary package commands.
remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions where practical and require explicit user confirmation before running npm, npx, codemod, or bootstrap commands.

remediation.issue: Starter app fetches public JSONPlaceholder data by default.
remediation.suggestion: Replace placeholder network calls with local mock data, or clearly document the outbound demo request before users run the starter app.

content.value_statement: Next.js 16 changes routing, caching, middleware, and build defaults. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code practical setup, migration, and architecture guidance.
actual_capabilities: Scaffolds Next.js 16 project structure with App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, and Turbopack defaults.
Guides migrations from middleware.ts to proxy.ts and from synchronous request APIs to awaited APIs.
Explains Cache Components, cacheLife, cacheTag, Suspense boundaries, and streaming composition.
Provides starter app files for pages, layouts, loading states, error states, proxy guards, and config.
Includes advanced patterns for auth, Server Actions, revalidation, product pages, dashboards, and blogs.
Supplies a PowerShell bootstrap script for Node, npm, codemod, and create-next-app workflows.
limitations: It focuses on Next.js 16 App Router projects, not Pages Router applications.
Some examples use placeholder APIs and abstract database helpers that require project-specific replacement.
The bootstrap script depends on Node.js, npm, npx, network access, and the public package registry.
Version-specific guidance should be checked against official Next.js release notes before production upgrades.

use_cases.title: Start a New App
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js 16 baseline with App Router, Turbopack, Tailwind, and recommended file structure.

use_cases.title: Upgrade an Existing App
use_cases.description: Plan a migration from Next.js 15 patterns to awaited request APIs, proxy.ts, and stable cache settings.

use_cases.title: Design Production Routes
use_cases.description: Apply streaming, Cache Components, auth guards, Server Actions, and cache invalidation to real workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Starter Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Next.js 16 Launchpad skill to plan a new App Router project with TypeScript, Tailwind, Turbopack, and Cache Components.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Next.js 16 Launchpad skill to review my Next.js 15 app and list required changes for proxy.ts, async params, and config updates.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Cached Route
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Next.js 16 Launchpad skill to design a cached product page with Suspense streaming, cache tags, and safe Server Actions.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Build Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Next.js 16 Launchpad skill to diagnose Turbopack, Cache Components, Suspense, and proxy.ts issues in this repository.

output_examples.input: Plan a new dashboard app with Next.js 16 defaults.
output: Recommended stack choices for Node, TypeScript, Tailwind, App Router, and Turbopack.
A concise project structure with app routes, proxy guard, loading state, and error state.
Setup steps that identify package commands requiring user confirmation.

output_examples.input: Migrate my middleware and params usage to Next.js 16.
output: A migration checklist for middleware.ts to proxy.ts.
Guidance for awaited params, searchParams, cookies, headers, and draft mode APIs.
Testing notes for protected routes and streaming boundaries.

output_examples.input: Design an e-commerce product page with cached reviews.
output: A route architecture using Server Components, Client Components, Suspense, and cache tags.
A data freshness plan for product data, reviews, and cart updates.
Security notes for auth checks, server-only data, and public environment variables.

best_practices: Confirm before running npm, npx, codemod, or bootstrap commands from the skill.
Replace placeholder APIs and database helpers with project-specific services before deployment.
Use Suspense, server-only boundaries, and explicit cache lifecycles for production routes.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for Pages Router projects without adapting the guidance.
Do not run @latest or @canary package commands in production without review.
Do not copy placeholder auth, API, or database examples without adding validation and tests.

faq.question: Does this skill create a complete production app?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance, starter files, scripts, and architecture patterns that need project-specific implementation.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it support Next.js 15 or older versions?
faq.answer: It is focused on Next.js 16. Older projects should use the migration guidance before applying patterns.

faq.question: Why are command confirmations important?
faq.answer: The skill includes npm, npx, codemod, and bootstrap workflows that can install packages and modify files.

faq.question: Can I use the starter app as-is?
faq.answer: Use it as a reference. Replace placeholder fetch URLs, auth checks, and styling with production choices.

faq.question: Does it cover security practices?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers server-only data, environment variable boundaries, proxy auth, input validation, and cache safety.
